guide.summary: Private app, your own workspace only (self-serve, wait none); Public app for other customers' workspaces (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app, your own workspace only (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for other customers' workspaces (app review).

composio.note: Composio supplies a managed OAuth app for Intercom, fine for prototypes. Users see Composio's name on the consent screen, and the quota is shared across all Composio users.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio manages an Intercom app. For production you will want your own app so users see your name, you control scopes, and you get dedicated quota. Customer-facing public apps need Intercom approval.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of Composio on the consent screen
Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not cover your needs
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets a dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace
prerequisites.detail: Private apps that access your own workspace require a paid workspace. Use of Intercom, even via a free platform account, requires the separate Intercom Customer Agreement.

prerequisites.title: Developer Hub account and OAuth enabled
prerequisites.detail: Follow Intercom's registration requirements for a developer account, then tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions for reviewers
prerequisites.detail: If your app needs an account or subscription, supply test credentials or setup instructions in the description.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can register several, including testing and production URLs.

steps.title: Generate private access token
steps.detail: In your paid workspace, generate an Access Token for your private app from the Intercom dashboard.
steps.done_when: You hold an access token for your workspace.

steps.title: Create a staging app in Developer Hub
steps.detail: Intercom recommends a separate staging app for development. Tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page.
steps.done_when: OAuth is enabled on the staging app.

steps.title: Pick minimal scopes
steps.detail: Draft the smallest scope list that covers your agent's use case, with a justification for each. Webhook topics need matching scopes.
steps.done_when: Scope list and reasons are ready to enter.

steps.title: Register redirect URL and select scopes
steps.detail: Enter the HTTPS redirect URL and tick scopes in the Developer Hub. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Redirect URL and scopes are saved.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config for the intercom toolkit using your own client ID and secret from the Basic Information page.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Fill listing and partner pages
steps.detail: Complete the App Listing and App Partner Program pages, which ask for company details, use cases and contacts. Images must be marketing format, and the app name cannot contain Intercom.
steps.done_when: All Test and publish pages show complete.

steps.title: Record OAuth demo video
steps.detail: Show install with OAuth, full functionality, and uninstall, with the full client_id and state in the OAuth URL. Missing parts mean resubmission.
steps.done_when: Video covers install, features and uninstall.

steps.title: Submit app for review
steps.detail: Submit from the Test and publish section of the Developer Hub. Provide working installation links.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days. If changes are requested, fix them and resubmit.
steps.done_when: App is approved and becomes public unlisted.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes get apps rejected
traps.detail: This is the most common initial rejection reason. Intercom may also approve fewer permissions than you requested.

traps.title: Approval can be refused
traps.detail: Intercom may withhold approval, and may reject a listing application, in its sole discretion.

traps.title: Review can take longer than stated
traps.detail: A 2021 community post reports 15+ days with no response. Plan buffer time.

traps.title: Broken installation links cause rejection
traps.detail: Broken or unclear links in the Installation status section cause rejection and a full resubmission.

traps.title: Approved apps can be re-reviewed
traps.detail: Changes need re-approval, though the app stays public with current functionality meanwhile. Intercom may also review you at any time and revoke credentials if non-compliant.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app. Switch to your own app for production.

traps.title: Restrictions on how you build
traps.detail: You cannot build a product competing with Intercom, resell Intercom data, or use end user data for advertising targeting.

blockers.symptom: App rejected for scopes outside current functionality
blockers.what_it_means: You requested more scopes than the app uses.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove extra scopes and resubmit; allow up to seven more business days.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the requested scopes with actual API calls and propose a smaller set.

blockers.what_it_means: The video did not show all functionality and the OAuth processes.
blockers.what_to_do: Re-record covering install, all features, and uninstall, showing the full client_id and state.

open_questions: Whether customer workspace admins must approve the app on install is not stated; the docs only mention the authorizing user. Ask Intercom developer support or test an install with a non-admin user.
Current real-world review times are only documented as up to seven business days, plus a 2021 report of 15+ days. Ask in the Intercom developer community.
Cost of listing is unknown; Intercom reserves the right to charge fees. Check the App Partner Program terms.
Whether Intercom's redirect-URI handling needs the Composio callback proxy is unconfirmed.

evidence.answer: Intercom has sole editorial control of the App Store and may remove developer apps at any time without notice.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: (c) use Developer Credentials with any Developer App other than the Developer App for which Intercom issued such Developer Credentials
evidence.answer: Developer Credentials may be used only with the app for which Intercom issued them.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: You will see a yellow banner at the top of the screen stating it can take up to seven business days for review.
evidence.answer: Intercom's official docs state review can take up to seven business days.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: If you have requested scopes outside of the current functionality, you may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app.
evidence.answer: A common review blocker is requesting scopes beyond what the app actually uses, which can force a scope change and resubmission.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Providing broken or unclear links will result in an application rejection, and you will have to resubmit for review.
evidence.answer: Broken or unclear installation links in the Installation status section cause rejection and a full resubmission.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Our team submitted an app 15 days ago and haven't yet received a review.
evidence.answer: Community report (2021): a developer waited 15+ days with no review, well past the stated seven business days, and had to escalate via the forum.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Good news! If you are planning on keeping that app private then no need to submit for review.
evidence.answer: Support engineer (2022): private apps need no review; review is only needed for installs in other workspaces, and OAuth redirect and webhook URLs must be in place at submission but can be changed later.
